lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Claudette, this is Kendra. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to cook at home 5 nights. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than I thought. 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to stop eating out so much.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the cooking at home going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, no, not really. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, sometimes. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the cooking at home going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I got home late every day this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe cook at home 3 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 8. Maybe 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 8 and not a 5?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can cook on Sunday and have it for a few days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If work gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: finding the time made this week harder, you still got 5 days in, and your plan is to cook at home 3 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Reflects openness and wish for fit
Desire to feel like herself again; not explored
Commits to doing it this week

flags.reason: Health-threat warning pushed without permission; MI non-adherent and fear-based.
'You have to stop' is a directive that undercuts autonomy after participant reported barriers.
Repeats the same open question after participant named time barriers at line 41; the barrier was not explored.
Third verbatim repeat of the 'how would things be different' question; participant answers were not reflected back.

score.summary: Coach reviewed the prior goal, elicited a realistic 3-night goal with confidence rating, and planned for a barrier with a backup plan and a clear summary. However, coach used two directive warnings and repeated the same question three times without reflecting the participant's barriers, which weakened partnership.
strengths: Line 8 and 11: affirmed the 5-day success and follow-through.
Line 15: emphasized that the plan is the participant's own choice.
Line 37 and 39: affirmed the participant's self-generated barrier solution and schedule knowledge.
Line 56: clear summary that confirmed the participant's plan before closing.
coaching_tips: Replace line 20 ('You have to stop eating out') with a question asking permission or inviting the participant's ideas, e.g., 'Would it help to talk about eating out?'
Reflect the time barrier at line 41 before asking again; the repeated question at line 42 and 46 ignored it.
Explore the change talk at line 14 ('I want to feel like myself again') with a follow-up open question rather than moving on.
Avoid the health-threat warning at line 16; reflect the participant's frustration with others' warnings instead, as at line 17.
